validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE strongly confirmed and NOT a duplicate. Independent corroboration across four origin classes: (1) EIA Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook, Aug2026 release, 'Historical Projects' sheet row 1195 (operator Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Company LLC entry) -- Completed, in-service 2025, LA, 174 mi, 30/36/42 in, 1800 MMcf/d, docket CP24-122-000; (2) two independent secondary write-ups of FERC's Sept 27 2024 order (Van Ness Feldman via natlawreview.com, and naturalgasintel.com) describing a 1.8 Bcf/d, 174-mile, 30-42in system with ~775 wellpad receipt points on the Haynesville Spine + Juniper South segments; (3) Williams' own SEC 10-Q filings for Q3 2025 (filed 2025-11-03) and Q2 2026 (filed 2026-08-03), which report LEG revenue inside the West segment and state it 'was placed into service in the third quarter of 2025' / 'in July and August 2025'; (4) trade press (pgjonline.com, ogj.com x2) on FID (Jun 2022), construction resumption (Aug 2024) and startup (Jul 23-25 2025, initial flows into Transco at Beauregard Parish LA). Not a duplicate of P6843 LEAP Expansion Phase 4 (different owner/operator -- DT Midstream, not Williams; different system, EIA's own adjacent row 1194) nor of P0285 Haynesville Global Access (cancelled, different sponsor) -- they are separate egress systems that happen to share the Haynesville-to-Gillis corridor and Gillis Hub delivery point; EIA lists LEG, LEAP Phase 4, and a third unrelated system (Momentum Midstream's NG3, not a GEM row) as three distinct completed 2025 projects in the same corridor. Route geometry at ../GOIT-GGIT-pipeline-routes/data/individual-routes/gas-pipelines/P5115.geojson (15-point single LineString) runs from about (-93.95, 32.15) near Logansport/Haynesville-shale far-north LA down to about (-93.20, 30.46) in the Gillis-hub area of southwest LA (Calcasieu/Beauregard Parish) -- an accurate trace of the sourced Haynesville-to-Gillis corridor; no route-vs-sheet mismatch. Capacity (1800 MMcf/d), Diameter (30/36/42 in) as recorded agree with EIA and the FERC-order write-ups (see fills). Only open items: PipelineType is misclassified (separate concern below); ProposalYear/Pressure/SegmentCost could not be sourced (UNRESOLVED, see fills, with what was searched).

validity.recommendation: reclassify PipelineType from 'transmission' to 'gathering' -- FERC's own jurisdictional ruling on this exact system
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's current PipelineType='transmission' is supported only by a citation to eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php#pipelines, a navigation page that does not name this pipeline (builder's own relevance check: name_found=false) -- so the value was effectively uncited, not merely under-cited. Independent, on-point evidence says the opposite: on 2024-09-27 FERC issued an Order on Petition for Order to Show Cause (Energy Transfer LP's petition, docket proceedings around CP24-122) applying the 'primary function test' and finding the LEG System -- despite its large 30-42in diameter and high operating pressure, both typical of transmission -- is legally and functionally a GATHERING system: a spine-like configuration gathering unprocessed gas from ~775 wellhead receipt points along its length, with no FERC NGA jurisdiction. Reported independently by a law firm (Van Ness Feldman, via natlawreview.com) and by trade press (naturalgasintel.com, 'Williams Prevails as FERC Rules Louisiana LEG System a Natural Gas Gathering Pipe'), both describing the same primary document with matching specifics (174 mi, 1.8 Bcf/d, 775 receipt points). Williams' own SEC 10-Qs likewise describe LEG only as 'natural gas gathering assets' / 'gathering system', never as an interstate transmission line. `gathering` is a valid value in the repo's controlled vocabulary (docs/reference/controlled_vocab.md). This is a genuine misclassification, not a close call -- FERC's order is a formal jurisdictional determination on this exact system.

cross_row_leads.facts: EIA 'Historical Projects' sheet row 1194: 'Louisiana Energy Access Project (LEAP) Expansion Phase 4', operator DTE (DT Midstream), Expansion, Completed, in-service 2025-09; 150 mi total system / 36 in, +200 MMcf/d incremental capacity (raising LEAP total from 1.9 to 2.1 Bcf/d); FID October 2024; FERC affirmed LEAP's gathering status September 2024 (same primary-function-test finding as LEG, separate docket); delivers Haynesville supply to the Gillis Hub and Gulf Coast LNG markets. Distinct system from P5115 LEG -- different owner/operator (DT Midstream vs Williams) -- not a duplicate, but the two systems are close analogues (both FERC-affirmed Haynesville-to-Gillis gathering spines that went in service within weeks of each other in 2025).

status_reviews.researcher_notes: The sheet's 'construction' (updated=2025-10-15, presumably still reflecting the pre-startup Reuters/S&P Global sources) is now stale by at least three months. Independent evidence: (1) trade press reports initial flows of 75 MMcf/d on 2025-07-23 into Transco at Beauregard Parish LA, rising to ~145 MMcf/d by 2025-07-25; (2) Williams' own Q3 2025 10-Q (filed 2025-11-03) states LEG 'was placed into service in July and August 2025'; (3) Williams' Q2 2026 10-Q (filed 2026-08-03) confirms 'a full year of the Louisiana Energy Gateway expansion project' contributing to 2026 growth and states it 'was placed into service in the third quarter of 2025'. EIA's Aug2026 workbook lists 'Completed' with a 2025-10-01 completed-date (likely full-capacity ramp rather than first service). Recommending Status=operating, StartYear1=2025, StartMonth1=7 (first flows). Note the FERC ruling (Sept 2024) also means this system is a non-jurisdictional intrastate/gathering line, not a certificated interstate project -- consistent with why there is no FERC in-service notice to cite; the operator disclosures (10-Qs) and press substitute for that in the source ladder as expected for an intrastate/gathering line.
